events.description: Take a docent led tour of the Conference House Museum also known as the Billiopp House located on Staten Island, New York and overlooking the Raritan Bay. This two-story grand fieldstone house was built by powerful landowner Royal Navy Captain Christopher Billopp About 1680. He wanted a home that would be an expression of his massive wealth, as well as a symbol of the stability of the colonies.  Nearly a century later the Billopp House had become a center of colonial hospitality. Billopp’s great-grandson, loyal to the crown, offered his ancestral family home as the site of a meeting of great importance.It is Named The Conference House because it is the site of the only Peace Conference of the American Revolution. Continental Congress representatives Benjamin Franklin, John Adams and Edward Rutledge met here with British Admiral Lord Howe at his request on September 11,1776 in an unsuccessful effort to stop the American Revolution. The Americans had already written and signed the Declaration of Independence on July 4,1776 and their course would not be altered. Though the group discusses options for a peaceful cessation of hostilities, no agreement was reached and the fighting continued for seven years.Today the Conference House Museum presents an interpretation of an 18th century colonial manor to the general public. The building is owned by NYC Parks and operated by the Conference House Association as a historic house museum in partnership with the Historic Trust of NYC.

events.description: Set within the living landscape of 6BC Botanical Garden, this third annual iteration, curated by Sarah Viviana Valdez, brings together the sculptural practices of Ori Carlin, Erin Lingard, and Lizzy Chemel. The artists span materials and techniques, notably including wood-fired ceramics, metal, concrete, salvaged materials and stained glass mirages. Their works share a common sentiment toward incredible craftsmanship deriving from botany, memory, and family histories. Throughout the garden's labyrinth, each location and placement of these pieces will similarly act as an embroidery unifying the rhythms and quiet transformations to shape their own narratives. Beginning in the afternoon and unfolding toward sundown, the exhibition will culminate with closing performances by Sky Axe, Karol Konstancia with ensemble, and Fillan Fernando. These performers honor traditions of myth, folklore, songwriting, choral a cappella, and poetry. The intent is to offer gifts that extend the exhibition’s exploration of memory and storytelling. We invite visitors to wander through a space where sculpture, sound, and movement become small openings into remembrance and shared imagination. For folks who feel compelled, the curator will offer tours throughout the day. Enjoy these presented moments of pause where the private worlds we carry within us are invited to briefly open onto the garden and one another.

events.description: Yoga Nidra, also known as “yogic sleep,” is a guided meditation practice designed to bring you into a state of deep relaxation while remaining fully aware. This powerful practice helps release stress, restore balance, and promote profound healing by guiding you through layers of consciousness—moving from wakefulness to a dream-like state and into deep rest. No experience is needed—simply lie down, get comfortable, and allow yourself to be guided into deep stillness. Whether you’re looking to ease tension, improve sleep, or reconnect with yourself, Yoga Nidra offers a space for complete rest and renewal. All levels are welcome.

events.description: Solo and group exhibitions at Glyndor Gallery explore the dynamic relationships between nature, culture, and site. Registration is not required for this drop-in event. Today’s tour features current exhibitions. Questions? Please email us at information@wavehill.org or call 718.549.3200 x251.    Glyndor Gallery is wheelchair-accessible. There is an accessible, ground-level entrance at the front of the building with an elevator that provides access to the gallery level. The Sunroom Project Space can be accessed with an ADA-compliant ramp. The restroom on the gallery level is all-gender and ADA-compliant.

events.description: Celebrate National Dance Day with a guided walk through Fort Tryon Park featuring dance, live music & poetry!Meet at Broadway and Dongan Place Entrance at 3PM | Audience Members Guided Through the Park On Wheelchair Accessible Pathways | Walking ProductionCelebrate National Dance Day with an immersive, multi-disciplinary arts production in Fort Tryon Park! A guided walk through the park leads audience members to view Uptown Dance Collective’s (UDC) “Alterations and Repairs: Nature and Us” with dance, music, and spoken word all woven into the landscape of the parkland. Audience members will also take a little journey to Brazil and learn Samba dance at the end of the walk and some Bomba from Puerto Rico along the way.UDC dance artists Lisa Green, Amy Kail, Navarra Novy-Williams will be joined by Shanik Garcia, Juan Usera, Paul Thompson, and Rishauna Zumberg. This group of dance artists collectively draw from diverse traditions including Afro-Brazilian, Afro-Puertorican, and European and U.S. Modern Dance in creating and performing their dances. John Ehlis, Matthew Gonzales, and Jessica Lurie perform original music on Saxophone, Flute, Guitar, and Drums; and poets Alison Stone and Peter Bulow share poems created for the day. Alexis Camacho, Victoria Lopez, and Valerie Quito from The Center Dance Studio in Inwood will also join us this year!We encourage our audience to bring light pillows, blankets, or folding chairs you can easily carry as we go from site to site.“Alterations and Repairs: Nature and Us” is made possible with support from The City Parks Foundation’s Green Fund, The Harkness Foundation for Dance, The Greenacre Foundation, and The Medical Center Neighborhood Fund. This event brings the arts to the outdoors—inviting you to witness, move and connect.Click Here to go to Uptown Dance Collective’s WebsiteRain date: Saturday September 26

E-waste items collected at these events include: household and office electronics (computers, laptops, keyboards, printers), smaller entertainment electronics (video game consoles, cell phones, MP3 players), and TVs, VCRs, DVDs, DVRs.

Textile items include: clothing, shoes, hats, bags, gloves, towels, curtains, bedding, and all clean, dry, unsoiled fabrics.

categories: Tenant Resource Fair ,Free,Property Owner Clinic,Property Owner Resource Fair,Education,General Events,Housing Ambassador Event,General Events,HPD Outreach Event
events.description_html:
Under the Asthma-Free Housing Act (Local Law 55 of 2018), residential building owners in New York City are required to take steps to keep their buildings free of mice, rats, roaches and mold, collectively defined as Indoor Allergens. In this training, we will discuss owners' responsibilities to identify and eliminate indoor allergen hazards and other pests, as well as review the annual inspection requirements, when to use a licensed contractor, and how to clear HPD violations. Space is limited – please register now.

Topics include:

  • Eliminating and preventing infestations of mice, rats, cockroaches, and other pests;
  • Identifying current and future sources of mold;
  • Proper work methods for eliminating mold conditions and pest infestations;
  • Reviewing the city and state laws that underlie the Asthma-Free Housing Act;
  • Annual notification and inspection requirements and the annual Bedbug Filing (Local Law 69 of 2017); and
  • Steps to correct and remove HPD violations for Indoor Allergen Hazards.
events.short_description: Pests and Mold: An Owners Guide to Indoor Allergen Laws
events.title: Pests and Mold: An Owners Guide to Indoor Allergen Laws

events.address: Van Cortlandt Classic Playground in Van Cortlandt Park
events.description_html: New location for September. Forest Fridays are meeting at Classic Playground, not the Learning Garden.<br \/>Help restore the woodland edge at Van Cortlandt Park. Volunteers remove the invasive shrubs and vines crowding out young native trees - multiflora rose, bush honeysuckle, porcelain berry, jetbead and ivy - and tend a small native planting put in this June. Hand tools only. Tools, gloves and guidance provided; no experience needed.<br \/>Dates include Fridays weekly from September 4th - September 25th. Dates are 9\/4, 9\/11, 9\/18, and 9\/25.<br \/>Meet at the public restroom building inside Classic Playground, at Van Cortlandt Park South and Gouverneur Avenue. The worksite is right at the playground, so latecomers can find us.<br \/>Wear long sleeves, long trousers and sturdy closed-toe shoes. Bring water. Ages 15+ welcome; minors need a waiver.<br \/><a href=\"https:\/\/volunteer.bloomerang.co\/volunteer\/#\/join-party?k=9iode48dd17tlw\">Sign up on Bloomerang<\/a><br \/>

events.title: Forest Fridays: Volunteer Forest Restoration at Van Cortlandt Park

events.address: Kissena Park
events.description_html: Volunteer with the Stewardship Team to protect the forested areas in Kissena Park! Volunteers will contribute to ongoing restoration work and learn the importance of species diversity to ecosystem health. Come dressed in sturdy boots or shoes, long sleeves, long pants, and clothing that can get dirty. Face masks may be worn at your discretion. Space is limited and registration is required. Volunteers under 18 must be accompanied by a chaperone. This event has been made possible with funds from the U.S. Department of Agriculture, Forest Service. To sign up a group of 10 or more volunteers please reach out to stewardship@parks.nyc.gov.<br \/>

The program is free and open to runners and walkers of all ages, abilities, and experience levels.<br \/>Evidence of Inwood Hill Park's formation exists as caves, valleys, and ridges left as the result of shifting glaciers. events.address: Broadway\/Arden Entrance in Fort Tryon Park
events.description_html: Join the Fort Tryon Park Conservancy and NYC Parks for cleaning in Fort Tryon Park! Help beautify the park along the Broadway Promenade. Meet at the Broadway Greeting Garden at the Arden Street\/Broadway entrance. Wear long pants, sturdy shoes, and get ready to improve the park's ecology by removing debris and helping site preparations.  Tools and gloves will be provided but please bring a filled water bottle.<br \/>Groups of 5+ must RSVP by emailing john.kelly@parks.nyc.gov 2 weeks in advance.<br \/>Volunteers under age 18 must be accompanied by an adult.<br \/>Beautification Days along the eastern expanse of the park take place on the 2nd & 4th Saturdays of each month from March to November. The Fort Tryon Park Conservancy supports these volunteer opportunities by underwriting tools, horticultural supplies, and NYC Parks staffing to oversee projects.<br \/>
events.short_description: Join the Fort Tryon Park Conservancy & NYC Parks for a Beautification Day! Help remove debris and improve the park's ecology along the Broadw
events.title: Broadway Beautification

events.address: BPL- Macon Library
events.description_html: A welcoming exercise class focused on helping participants feel stronger, more mobile, and more energized in daily life. Class includes low-impact strength and endurance exercises, mobility training, functional fitness and balance work. Modifications will be provided for all levels of fitness.

events.description_html: This high-energy total body workout will keep you moving with challenging yet fun bodyweight circuits. events.address: Audubon Center at the Boathouse in Prospect Park
events.description_html: A 45-minute dance fitness class to your favorite upbeat pop songs! Come prepared to shake, roll, grapevine, and clap. We will use this time to cultivate joy and silliness while getting a great workout and reaping the benefits of cardiovascular fitness. All levels are welcome and encouraged. Whether you want to learn some new choreography or need a space to step-touch and sing, this class is for you!

events.address: Wave Hill
events.description_html:
Ever wanted to see the world through an animal's eyes? Join us for a project in collaboration with Wave Hill Winter Workspace artist Sari Carel, where families will have the opportunity to create their own map from the perspective of the many creatures that can be found on our grounds.  
 
Registration not required.  
 
Wave Hill House is wheelchair-accessible. There is an accessible, ground-level entrance at the front of the building with a power-assist door. The restroom on the ground level is all-gender and ADA-compliant. Additional ADA-compliant restrooms are available on the lower level, which can be accessed by elevator.
events.short_description: Ever wanted to see the world through an animal's eyes?
events.title: Family Art Project: Animal Mapmaking

events.address: Buddy Monument in Forest Park
events.description_html: Join NYC Parks and The Forest Park Trust for Forest Restoration this summer to engage in hands-on forest restoration work, including invasive species removal, trail restoration, and possible planting in our park.<br \/>Registration is required. All tools will be provided, and no prior experience is needed. Just bring your enthusiasm. Please come dressed in sturdy, closed-toe shoes and bring your own water bottle.<br \/>
events.short_description: Join NYC Parks and The Forest Park Trust for Forest Restoration this summer to engage in hands-on forest restoration work!
events.title: Forest Restoration at Buddy Monument

events.address: Concrete Park Boat Launch in Concrete Plant Park
events.description_html: Join us for a guided Estuary Paddle on the Bronx River!<br \/>This guided canoe tour starts and ends at the Concrete Plant Park boat launch. It takes paddlers through the lower saltwater portion of the river (to the river mouth and back), featuring a duality of estuarine and urban habitat. A great opportunity for birders to see a wide variety of shorebirds that call the Bronx home!<br \/>*Please note that this section of the river is influenced by tides, current, and winds. Due to variable river conditions and the possibility of encountering some boat traffic, we limit this paddle to participants aged 14 years or older. This is an intermediate level paddle and we recommend that paddlers have some basic canoe or kayak experience for this particular trip.<br \/>We will provide boats, paddles, PFDs, and a basic paddling safety orientation prior to getting on the water.<br \/>
events.short_description: Join us for a guided Estuary Paddle on the Bronx River!
events.title: Guided Estuary Paddle

events.address: Entrance - Franklin Avenue and Arnold Avenue in Jones Woods Park
events.description_html: Volunteer with the Stewardship team to protect the forested areas in Jones Woods Park! Volunteers will contribute to ongoing restoration work and learn the importance of species diversity to ecosystem health. Come dressed in sturdy boots or shoes, long sleeves, long pants, and clothing that can get dirty. Face masks may be worn at your discretion. Space is limited and registration is required. Volunteers under 18 must be accompanied by a chaperone. This event has been funded in part by NYC Service. To sign up a group of 10 or more volunteers please reach out to stewardship@parks.nyc.gov.<br \/>
events.short_description: Volunteers will contribute to ongoing restoration work and learn the importance of species diversity to ecosystem health.

events.address: Hart Island
events.description_html: Hart Island is the largest public cemetery in the country and has served New York City since 1869. Hart Island's history is connected to many communities with important stories to tell. During the South Island Tour, Rangers will explore what Hart Island meant to the people who lived there, worked there, and were\/are buried there. Walking the South Island includes discussion of an amusement park, military history, multiple pandemics, historic buildings and more. Join the Urban Park Rangers to hear their history and their voices.<br\/><br\/>Participants are chosen by lottery. <br\/><br\/>Lottery registration opens on Wednesday, September 16 and closes Thursday, September 17 at 11:59 p.m.<br\/><br\/><br\/>Please Note:<br\/>-You must register each member of your party for the lottery under the same account. Anyone who was not registered will not be permitted to attend.<br\/><br\/>-  If you are selected for the program, you will receive a series of emails confirming your selection and must respond...

events.description_html: Immerse yourself in the wonders of the night sky every Tuesday on the High Line! events.address: Woodlawn Playground in Van Cortlandt Park
events.description_html: Hands-on forest restoration in the Northeast Forest at Woodlawn. We remove the invasive plants crowding out the young native trees regenerating here, and protect what is already coming back. Tools, gloves and guidance provided - no experience needed. Meet at Woodlawn Playground; we walk in together.<br \/>Dates include Wednesdays weekly from September 2nd - September 30th. Dates are 9\/2, 9\/9, 9\/16, 9\/23, and 9\/30.<br \/>Space is limited to 30 volunteers each week. Groups of 6 or more should email noel@vancortlandt.org. Ages 15+ welcome; minors need a waiver.<br \/><a href=\"https:\/\/volunteer.bloomerang.co\/volunteer\/#\/join-party?k=koot8cmyrxtx16\">Register for a session<\/a><br \/>

events.address: Randall's Island Park
events.description_html: Volunteer with Team RIVER (Randall's Island Volunteer Ecological Restorers) and help keep Randall's Island Park beautiful! Team RIVER Volunteers regularly work with the Natural Areas team twice a month to take care of and restore our natural spaces on the island. With our Horticulture team, volunteers care for the many gardens, green streets and meadows, every second Wednesday of each month. Team RIVER also works with our Sports Field and Operations teams, keeping our park clean and maintained. If you are only able to volunteer on a limited basis, you are still very much welcome!<br \/>This volunteer opportunity is open to individuals from the community. Groups of more than 5 people must contact: <a href=\"mailto:Volunteers@RandallsIsland.org\">Volunteers@RandallsIsland.org<\/a><br \/>Volunteers must be at least 11 years old. Anyone under the age of 18 must have a waiver signed by their legal guardian before starting any work. Children under 16 must also have an adult with them while v...

events.description_html:
In recent years NYC has seen increased interest in developing affordable housing on land owned by faith-based organizations (FBOs) and other mission-driven organizations (MDOs).  These series of classes are designed to walk participants step-by-step through the development process and help them establish necessary connections within relevant government agencies.

Our goal is to educate FBOs about the housing development process, explain how City agencies are involved in that process, outline what to expect when working with various City agencies, and provide support and available resources.

  • What should I be thinking about as I start on this project?
  • What are the potential benefits of developing affordable housing for my institution and my wider community? What are the potential drawbacks or risks, financial or otherwise?
  • How long should I expect this process to take? What are the stages and who will my partners be?
  • How do I make the determination that my property might be a good candidate for housing?
